page: Hetzner Cloud cpx62 is an x86_64 virtual machine running on the QEMU hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC processors running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, with 16 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 640 GB NVMe SSD, while no dedicated GPU hardware is included.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, falls within the average range. Memory performance is notable, with large-block read and write bandwidths, as well as the Passmark memory score, ranking in the top 25%. The server also demonstrates strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and strong text generation speeds for small and medium language models.

The shared CPU allocation presents a performance tradeoff, as resources are shared with other tenants, which may introduce variability under sustained multi-core loads. However, this shared architecture offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong single-core performance, this server is suited for web serving, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and light LLM inference workloads.
